★ THE_SPAN_LAYER_IS_THE_ANSWER.what_is_missing: SPAN CONSTRUCTION — deriving, from raw morphology, the addressable term-in-verse spans that everything above joins on. That is the pre-processing before lexical.
why_it_is_the_load-bearing_gap: plan §3.4.2 states it outright: 'the span-id IS the join key' — never Strong's-encoded endpoints
ent.lexical.record identity = span-id + ve_nr — every lexical read is ABOUT a span
ent.char.candidate identity = span-id — every candidate IS a span
ve_lexical.from_span / to_span — every pair's endpoints are spans
So the entire interpretation layer is addressed in a currency no process mints.
★ THE_SPAN_LAYER_IS_THE_ANSWER.where_it_lives_today: Inside `audit_word`, which 'inserts + span-links terms and verses in one pass' (CLAUDE.md §8) — bundled with ingest, and reachable by a flag literally named `--skip-span-backpop`.
★ THE_SPAN_LAYER_IS_THE_ANSWER.⚠ why_that_is_dangerous: A step everything joins on is SKIPPABLE, undocumented as a process, and has no gate of its own. `span_strong_match` is the field that proves a term is actually AT a verse — the difference between evidence and a reference — and it is produced by a bundled side-effect. A skipped backpop leaves spans absent; absent spans leave the lexical layer with nothing to read; and nothing announces it.
★ THE_SPAN_LAYER_IS_THE_ANSWER.the_layer_violation: Span construction is DERIVATION from morphology, so by raw.definition it is BASE, not raw. Bundling it into the ingest module puts a base artefact inside a raw process — the same layer-mixing the plan forbids (§3.4.2 'no analytical values on mechanical tables'), one layer down.

★ the_gap_the_researcher_found.what_this_file_does_about_it: It states the modules and the wiring, and marks modules 4 and 8 (and the missing span module) explicitly rather than quietly omitting them. Whether to carve the base layer into processes is a researcher decision — see open.pipeline.base-layer-carve. This file does not pretend the gap is closed.

RULED_20260715.the_ruling: researcher 2026-07-15: 'the registry create the starting point (this is also not yet in configurator). raw pulls STEP and create the tables with the STEP data. No data conversion. Base then processes the data and prepare it for the lexical analysis. This requires master, char seed, and passages to be in place. With signoff of the base, the lexical analysis can start.'
RULED_20260715.the_stage_chain: REGISTRY -> RAW -> BASE -> [SIGNOFF] -> LEXICAL -> CHARACTERISTICS -> FINDINGS
what_it_settled: BASE IS ONE PROCESS, not three. My recommendation of three (spans/stems/passages) is OVERRULED, and the reason matters: I carved by WHAT IS PRODUCED; the researcher carves by WHEN IT IS DONE. A stage is a unit of COMPLETION — and base's completion is a signoff.
`verses-passages` RETIRED -> `base`. Passages are a base OUTPUT; treating one artefact of the stage as a peer of the stage was the carve error.
THE SEED IS BASE. char.seed-layers + ent.char.candidate moved out of characteristics -> process/base.json. Resolves open.pipeline.seed-layer-home.
SPANS ARE BASE, and now have a home (base.spans) and a gate (gate.base.span-master-complete) rather than being an audit_word side-effect behind --skip-span-backpop.
REGISTRY IS THE STARTING POINT and was missing entirely -> process/registry.json.
★ A HUMAN SIGNOFF GATES LEXICAL — the pipeline's only human gate (gate.base.signoff).
RULED_20260715.why_the_signoff_is_the_important_part: It is what makes base a STAGE rather than a bag of derivations. Base is also the last point where a defect is CHEAP: after it, everything is interpretation, and an error in the span master or the seed does not surface as a bad span — it surfaces as a wrong reading, months later, indistinguishable from a bad read. The 2026-07-14 audit could not tell those apart.

meta.the_flow: REGISTRY (0) -> {FETCH+RAW (1)} -> BASE (2: spans, stem master, char seed, passages) -> [SIGNOFF] -> LEXICAL (5) -> CHARACTERISTICS (6) -> VALIDATION (7) -> ANALYSIS-PREP (8) -> FINDINGS (9). Arrows are DEPENDENCIES, not hard-coded calls (plan §3.2). The signoff is the only HUMAN gate in the chain.

open.issue: The base layer (spans · passages · stems · seeds) has one process for passages, none for spans or stems, and its seeds sit inside an interpretation process. The `governs` vocabulary has no value for spans or stems, so a module for them cannot even declare what it governs.
open.consequence: The pre-processing between raw and lexical is unconfigured and therefore ungoverned — no rules, no gates, no home. It is also the step the whole interpretation layer's addressing depends on.
options: A: ONE `base` process — spans + stems + passages + seeds together. Simple; but it swallows `verses-passages`, which is already authored and has real genre-routing rules of its own, and it makes one process own four unrelated derivations.

B: THREE processes — add `spans` and `stems` alongside the existing `verses-passages`; seeds stay with `characteristics`. Keeps the existing carve, mirrors the module list (3 = passages, 4 = stems, + a new span module), and each has genuinely different rules.

C: spans fold into `raw` — treat span-linking as part of ingest, as audit_word does today. REJECTED: spans are DERIVED, so by raw.definition they are base, and raw.immutable would then govern a derived artefact that changes whenever its derivation rule changes.
open.recommendation: B. Spans and stems have nothing in common except being derived: a span is an ADDRESS (the join key for everything above), a stem is a LINGUISTIC DERIVATION. Bundling them under one `base` process would produce exactly the kind of catch-all that the failure record calls over-structuring. C is how it works today and is precisely what hides the step.
open.resolve_by: researcher decision — BLOCKS a complete pipeline; modules 4 and the span module cannot declare `governs` until it is ruled
open.decision: OPTION A — one `base` process. Overrules my recommendation of B (three processes).
open.rationale: Base is a STAGE, and a stage is a unit of completion. The four artefacts (span master, stem master, char seed, passages) always run together, always for the same scope, and are only ever FINISHED together — because they finish at one signoff. Carving them into three processes would have split one stage across three homes that could never be independently done.

open.issue: The candidate seed is BASE per plan §3.4.1 ('Base — derived: passages, stems, seed/candidate stamping | Regenerate'), but char.seed-layers and ent.char.candidate live in process/characteristics.json, an interpretation process.
open.consequence: An interpretation process owns a base artefact. Already flagged from the other side in characteristics.json (ent.char.candidate: 'layer: base (mechanical seed) — but the screen0 verdict is INTERPRETATION and must not live on this row').
open.recommendation: Split by layer, not by topic: the mechanical seed (which spans are candidates) is BASE; the Screen-0 verdict and the role (what a candidate IS) are INTERPRETATION. They are already two facts on one row, which is the actual defect — the live DB stamps role/char_candidate onto verse_span_index, and the migration strips exactly that (plan 3.4.1).
open.decision: The seed is BASE. char.seed-layers + ent.char.candidate -> process/base.json; Screen-0/role stay in characteristics.
open.decided_by: researcher le Roux Cilliers, 2026-07-15 (implied by "base... requires master, char seed, and passages to be in place")

open.issue: Module 8 (Prepare data for analysis) governs no process. Prose (layer 4) has neither a process nor a module — the nine end at findings.
open.consequence: The study's END POINT is two-part: an evidenced findings corpus AND the products drawn from it (essays, study guides, books). The second part has no pipeline at all.
open.recommendation: Defer both, deliberately and on the record. The plan itself parks them ('Analysis & findings (least-defined): the study's higher-order outputs sit beyond segment 9'). Not a gap to close now — but it should be a KNOWN debt, not a silence, because it is half the stated end point.

open.issue: The researcher observed that raw and fetch are 'in the same pipeline'. They are: module 1 (Get data from STEP) performs both, and they are separate PROCESSES but not separate MODULES.
open.consequence: Not a defect — process and module are different axes and need not be 1:1. But it means module 1's post-gates must cover BOTH processes' controls, and a module that spans two processes loads two rule-sets.
open.recommendation: Keep them as one module and two processes, and let this be the worked example that process != module. Splitting them would gain nothing: a fetch that does not store is useless, and a raw write with no fetch cannot happen. The rules differ; the execution does not.
open.resolve_by: no decision needed — recorded so the asymmetry is deliberate

corrections_20260715.1_file_order: The modules array was not sorted by ordinal — module.registry (ordinal 0) sat SECOND, after ingest. Reading the file top-to-bottom, the starting point looked missing. It was not; it was out of order. Now sorted by ordinal, because a pipeline file that does not read in pipeline order is a pipeline file nobody can check.

2_ordinal_in_the_id.what_was_wrong: Ids embedded the ordinal (module.5.lexical, module.9.findings). After base absorbed the old modules 3 and 4, the sequence read 0,1,2,5,6,7,8,9 — gaps that look like missing modules.
2_ordinal_in_the_id.why_it_is_a_design_error: An ordinal CHANGES — reordering the pipeline is a config change, and this file has already reordered once today. An id is FROZEN AT MINT. Putting a mutable property inside an immutable id guarantees the id eventually lies. Exactly the defect already recorded as open.id-uniqueness (dim.114.reading was relabelled from 'discovery'; had the id carried the label as fact, it would now mislead).
2_ordinal_in_the_id.the_fix: Ids are now module.<name>. The ordinal lives in spec.ordinal, where it can change freely. An id says WHAT a thing is; never WHERE it currently sits.

★ the_step_anchors.the_ruling: researcher 2026-07-15: 'I think the pipeline should include anchors for all the processing units. we literally will have script references hanging off these processing units. a few simple examples: Registry: Create new item, Update tables, Validate; ingest: Get STEP for term by word/ Get step for term by Strong; Get related terms; Get verses, update tables, validate.'
★ the_step_anchors.what_a_step_is: The CONFIG/CODE BOUNDARY. Config says what the step IS, what it consumes, and what it must satisfy. The script says how. Plan §2.2: 'the code provides methods; the configurator provides the process' — the step is where those two meet, and until now there was no such place: a module bound to ONE handler (plan A.3 cfg_module.handler) with no way to say what happened inside it.
why_it_matters_more_than_it_looks: ADDRESSABLE — a step can be cited, gated, versioned, disabled and re-bound to a different script without touching the module. A step buried in a module's spec can do none of that.

IT MAKES THE BUNDLING VISIBLE — audit_word 'inserts + span-links terms and verses in one pass' is THREE steps in one script, across TWO layers (raw and base). With steps declared, that is legible; without them it is a sentence in a docstring.

IT IS THE REWRITE PLAN — plan §2.4 says existing scripts are a starting point 'expected to be substantially rewritten'. reference_script per step says exactly where each module's rewrite begins, and how much of an existing script belongs to which step.

★ the_pattern_in_the_researcher's_exampl.observation: Both examples end the same way: '...update tables, validate'. Registry = create new item, UPDATE TABLES, VALIDATE. Ingest = get by word / get by Strong / get related / get verses, UPDATE TABLES, VALIDATE.
★ the_pattern_in_the_researcher's_exampl.what_it_is: That is the plan's gated envelope (§3.2: 'pre-validate -> run -> post-validate -> checkpoint/track') expressed as steps. The work steps vary per module; the closing pair does not.
★ the_pattern_in_the_researcher's_exampl.so_it_is_a_rule_not_a_coincidence: EVERY module ends in update-tables then validate. Modelled explicitly (step.*.update-tables / step.*.validate) rather than left as a convention, because a convention is what the failure record calls 'a scan gate silently non-operational across whole books' — the step existed, nobody checked it ran.
★ the_pattern_in_the_researcher's_exampl.the_ordering_matters: update-tables comes BEFORE validate. The post-gate validates what was WRITTEN, not what was computed — otherwise it certifies an intention rather than a result.

terminology_alignment_20260715.authority: researcher ruling 2026-07-15 — align the process files with the pipeline's terminology; the terminology belongs in the enums (ruling a)

1_characteristic_to_characteristics.was: module.characteristic (singular) while the process, the governs value and process/characteristics.json are all PLURAL.
1_characteristic_to_characteristics.why_it_matters: It is one concept under two spellings. Every join, query and citation between the module and its process had to know which spelling applied where — and nothing checked. Trivial to fix, and exactly the kind of drift that is invisible until it is not.
1_characteristic_to_characteristics.now: module.characteristics; step.characteristics.*; the module, the process and the governs value all read the same.

2_scope_is_now_an_array.was: a STRING, and some values were 'book | cluster' / 'term | book' — TWO values pipe-jammed into one string.
2_scope_is_now_an_array.why_it_matters: Nothing could check it. A pipe-delimited multi-value is not a value; it is a sentence. Identical to the compound-shape defect in the dimensions (open.lexical.compound-shapes) and to the free-text `check` field — a controlled thing pretending to be prose.
2_scope_is_now_an_array.now: an ARRAY of enum.scope values. 8 values converted.

3_on_fail_retired_into_severity.was: module_gates carried `on_fail` (halt | warn) while every gate carries `severity` (red | amber). red MEANS halt; amber MEANS log-and-continue. One concept, two vocabularies.
3_on_fail_retired_into_severity.why_it_is_worse_than_untidy: It is not just a duplicate name — it is a DISCRETION HOLE. Two vocabularies for one concept means a module-gate binding could set on_fail=warn on a gate whose severity is red, silently downgrading a control at its point of use. 'Remove discretion / mechanical-first' is a named guardrail, and the failure record's clearest instance is a scan gate that was silently non-operational across whole books.
3_on_fail_retired_into_severity.the_ruling_applied: ONE nomenclature (ruling a) + no rule defined twice (ruling b3). A gate's severity is the gate's property and a binding may not override it. A gate that should halt in one module and warn in another is TWO GATES with two names, not one gate with a dial.
3_on_fail_retired_into_severity.now: 6 module_gates carry `severity` drawn from enum.severity. `on_fail` is gone.
3_on_fail_retired_into_severity.⚠ note: plan §A.3 defines cfg_module_gate.on_fail [halt|warn] AND cfg_gate.severity. The plan has the duplicate. This supersedes that column.

4_what_is_deliberately_NOT_aligned.module.ingest spans fetch+raw: One MODULE, two PROCESSES. Not a mismatch — process and module are different axes (open.pipeline.raw-fetch-coupling).
